newsitem.title: USA: Boeing settles dispute with Machinists union.
newsitem.headline: Boeing settles dispute with Machinists union.

text.p: Boeing Co. and its biggest union said Friday they have settled a dispute over the overlapping duties of certain hourly and salaried workers.
Under the settlement, 70 workers who have tranferred to salaried posts will get the right to return to hourly jobs represented by the Machinists Union, Boeing spokesman Peter Conte said.
The union charged Boeing was trying to eliminate some 800 to 1,200 hourly positions as part of an effort to streamline production processes in its commercial airplane group.
The National Labor Relations Board agreed with the union's complaint, and the issue was due to go before an administrative law judge next month.
"The company must understand we will never tolerate union-busting tactics here at Boeing," local President Bill Johnson said in a statement declaring the settlement a "huge victory" for the union.
Conte denied the company ever intended to remove jobs from the bargaining unit, although he said 15 workers voluntarily switched to salaried positions from similar hourly posts.
"This was never a union-busting tactic," Conte said. "We were not doing anything that was in violation of the bargaining agreement."

He said the agreement clarifies the distinction between salaried material planners and hourly "expediters," now known as materials processor requirements facilitators, who track work orders and airplane parts through the factory.
